status.en: 219 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Plateau State.
status.nb: 219 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Plateau State.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to carry out lethal attacks across Nigeria, killing an NSCDC officer and abducting a businessman in Plateau despite a curfew, and killing a woman and injuring two farmers in the same state. In Benue, Senate leaders are demanding a security overhaul after 113 people were killed, while electricity workers withdrew services in Makurdi following an alleged attack. Bandits killed seven vigilantes and abducted over 30 residents in Zamfara, and a terrorist strike in Borno killed 15 people. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å utføre dødelige angrep over hele Nigeria, dreper en NSCDC-offiser og bortfører en forretningsmann i Plateau til tross for portforbud, og dreper en kvinne og skader to bønder i samme delstat. I Benue krever senatledere en sikkerhetsreform etter at 113 personer ble drept, mens strømarbeidere avbrøt tjenestene i Makurdi etter et påstått angrep. Banditter drepte syv voktere og bortførte mer enn 30 innbyggere i Zamfara, og et terrorangrep i Borno drepte 15 personer. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
